Treatment options

Counsel offers most prescription weight loss medications. Whether you have a medication in mind or want to discuss options with your Counsel doctor, we can support your journey.

Zepbound® (tirzepatide)

Targets two hormones, mimicking the effects of both GLP-1 and GIP. It slows digestion and decreases appetite, which can help individuals eat less and lose weight.

Treatment
1 injection, once a week
Average weight loss
Up to 21% of body weight in clinical trials
Without insurance
$299/month*

Foundayo™ (orforglipron)

A GLP-1 medication, which the body naturally produces to regulate insulin and control blood sugar. It also works in the brain to curb food noise.

Treatment
1 tablet, once a day
Average weight loss
Up to 12% of body weight in clinical trials
Without insurance
$149/month*

Wegovy® (semaglutide)

Reduces hunger and cravings by targeting receptors in the gut and brain. It can help individuals eat less and lose weight.

Treatment
1 injection, once a week
Average weight loss
Up to 19% of body weight in clinical trials
Without insurance
$199/month*

Wegovy® pill (semaglutide)

Reduces hunger and cravings by targeting receptors in the gut and brain. It can help individuals eat less and lose weight.

Treatment

Average weight loss
Up to 15% of body weight in clinical trials

Hear from our members

Your questions, answered

Where is Counsel available?

Counsel is available in most U.S. states. GLP-1 prescribing is not currently available in Alabama, Louisiana, or New Jersey. Counsel, and therefore our weight management program, is not yet available in Arkansas, the District of Columbia, Kansas, Mississippi, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Washington, or West Virginia. If you live in one of these areas, you’ll join our waitlist and we’ll notify you when Counsel becomes available.

What if I get side effects?

That’s exactly what Counsel is built for. Side effects like nausea are common when starting a GLP-1 and can make it hard to stay on treatment. With Counsel, you get around-the-clock AI support plus access to a doctor who can respond in minutes, 7 days a week. If needed, your doctor can adjust your dose or change your treatment. You’re not left managing side effects on your own or waiting until your next appointment.

What does medication cost?

Medication prices are set by the manufacturers and vary by medication and pharmacy. The cash prices shown on our site use the latest available manufacturer coupons and are generally available at most major pharmacies. If you’re prescribed medication, you’ll be able to choose your pharmacy and see live cash prices for many major pharmacies before filling your prescription.

Do you help with insurance?

Counsel’s medical services are currently self-pay and are not reimbursable through insurance. We also do not currently support prior authorization workflows for medication coverage. Today, Counsel is best suited for members planning to pay cash for their medication. We plan to add more insurance support in the future.

I’m already on a GLP-1 from another platform. Can I switch?

Yes. Switching to Counsel is straightforward. During onboarding, we’ll ask about your current medication, dose, and the weight you were at when you started treatment. Otherwise, you’ll go through the same intake process as any other member so your Counsel doctor can understand your health history and treatment needs.

Can you treat things other than weight loss?

Yes. Counsel can help with acute, urgent, and primary care needs in addition to weight management. Counsel doctors can prescribe and refill medications, order labs and imaging, and provide referrals to specialists when appropriate. Your care doesn’t have to stop with weight loss.

How much does Counsel cost?

You can choose between two ways to pay: $300/year for unlimited doctor visits, or $29 per visit with no subscription. Medication and lab costs are separate.

Do you offer compounded medications?

No. Counsel only prescribes FDA-approved, brand-name weight-loss medications.

Do you support the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program?

Not yet. We’re exploring support for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program and hope to offer it in the future.

Will I need blood testing or lab work?

Yes. All new weight-management members complete initial lab testing. Labs cost about $18 in most states and $43 in New York and New Jersey.

Weight loss is connected to the rest of your health. Your care should be too.

Counsel considers your broader medical history, not just the number on a scale.
